Web Demos

stylesheet did not load — script did not run

Seven pages for the browser in this OS. Each one is a folder holding an index.html, a .css the page links to and a .js the page loads — nothing is inline, so opening a page proves the browser really fetches subresources next to it.

  • Hello JavaScript — a script runs, logs to the console and writes into the page while it is still being parsed.
  • Counter — real DOM click listeners; the readout repaints as the handler writes it.
  • Sketch — a <canvas> rasterised pixel by pixel in JavaScript and repainted from a timer, with no input at all.
  • Stopwatch — a setInterval rewriting a plain <div>, and laps built with createElement.
  • Todo — rows added and removed, and a counter that re-renders both its text and its class.
  • Paint — press and drag to draw: mousedown/mousemove/mouseup carrying real coordinates.
  • Events — what the browser delivers, and in what order: capture before bubble, keys at the focused field, change, submit.

These are editable copies. Change one and reload; to get the shipped version of a file back, delete your copy and run Add Default Icons from the desktop's right-click menu.
